narrative: Demand for PL2__M56CD6F1 shows a strong, statistically significant upward trend (slope +29.7 units/day, p<1e-15), shifting from ~2,500 units/day in Q1 2025 to over 6,500 units/day by Q1 2026. Lead times are unstable (CV=42%), driven primarily by transport variability, which inflates the lead-time demand sigma to 4,301 units. The current SAP safety stock of 2,780 is insufficient at a 95% service level; the model recommends raising it to 7,075. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy is chosen because the high and growing volume justifies real-time monitoring, and the EOQ of 29,366 units consolidates frequent small orders into ~25 annual replenishments, reducing ordering cost by 91%.
warnings: Demand trend is significant — safety stock and reorder point should be reviewed quarterly as the trend continues.
28 outliers (21.7%) detected; winsorisation applied at the 99th percentile.

research_insights.selection_rationale: High-volume, trending material with continuous daily consumption; continuous-review (r,Q) responds immediately to inventory depletion and is optimal when ordering costs are fixed and demand is non-stationary.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Safety stock increase from 2,780 to 7,075 units combined with EOQ of 29,366 yields a post-replenishment peak of 36,441 units — well within the 50,079-unit storage cap (72.8% utilisation). No capacity binding.
